output: Before exercise, eat something small with carbs and protein. Good options are a banana or a piece of whole grain bread with peanut butter. After exercising, focus on a balanced meal. Include protein, healthy fats, and whole grains. Always check with your doctor for personal advice.

output: Before exercise, eat something light and healthy. A small banana or a piece of whole grain bread is good. After exercising, have a meal with protein and carbs. Examples are chicken with brown rice or beans with vegetables. Always talk to your doctor for personal advice.

instruction: What specific actions can individuals with diabetes take to advocate for their own well-being during a healthcare visit?

instruction: What specific challenges might individuals with diabetes experience when trying to find specialized diabetes providers?
output: Finding specialized diabetes providers can be challenging due to factors such as limited availability in certain areas, long wait times for appointments, and difficulty navigating complex healthcare systems. This can lead to delays in diagnosis, treatment, and management of the condition.

instruction: What time of day is best to check my blood sugar?
output: It is good to check blood sugar in the morning before breakfast. This tells you your levels after fasting all night. You can also check after meals to see how food affects your sugar. Always talk to your doctor about the best times for you.

instruction: What types of healthy fats are beneficial for people with diabetes?
output: Individuals with diabetes should prioritize monounsaturated fats found in olive oil, avocados, nuts, and seeds. Additionally, polyunsaturated fats from fatty fish, flaxseeds, and walnuts are also beneficial.

instruction: When will I need to start using insulin for my type 2 diabetes?
output: Insulin may be needed if your blood sugar levels are too high. This can happen when diet and exercise alone do not help. Your doctor will check your blood sugar often. They will let you know if insulin is right for you.

instruction: Why do I need to visit the clinic regularly for my diabetes?
output: Regular clinic visits are important for managing diabetes. They help your doctor check your blood sugar levels. This way, they can see how well your treatment is working. It also allows you to ask questions and get support. Staying healthy is easier with regular check-ups!

instruction: Why does exercise help control my blood sugar?
output: Exercise helps your body use insulin better. Insulin is a hormone that controls blood sugar. When you move, your muscles need sugar for energy. This can lower your blood sugar levels. Try to stay active every day. Always talk to your doctor before starting a new exercise plan.

instruction: Why does my blood sugar go up after I eat?
output: When you eat food, your body breaks it down into sugar. This sugar enters your blood. Your blood sugar level rises because your body is using sugar for energy. Some foods raise blood sugar more than others. It's important to talk to your doctor about your diet.

instruction: Why does my blood sugar rise after I eat?

instruction: Why does sleeping well matter for my blood sugar control?

instruction: Why is it recommended for diabetic individuals to have regular dilated eye exams?
